cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster. It comes from when Nathan the prophet came to David after his adultery with Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite (2 Samuel 11:3). And every word of it, David says straight to God.

cards.question: After Nathan's visit, David turns to God. What's the very first thing David asks Him for?
David asks God for mercy. What does David lean on when he asks?

cards.text: Then David asks God to blot out his transgressions, wash him clean and cleanse him from his sin. Friend, that's not a rinse, that's the deluxe car wash with the hot wax AND the tire shine.

cards.question: True or false: David tells God he isn't sure what he did wrong.

cards.text: He knows EXACTLY what he did, and he says his sin is always before him. Like that 'reply all' you sent to the whole office by mistake, the one you see every time you close your eyes.

cards.question: Then David says who his sin is against. Who does he name?

cards.text: No excuses, no 'okay, but hear me out,' just this: he's done what is evil in God's sight. Me? One burnt batch and I'm blaming the oven, the timer AND the weather.

cards.question: David says he has sinned and done what is evil in God's sight, so that when God speaks, God may be proved ___.

cards.text: Then David looks back. Way, WAY back, further back than Bathsheba.

cards.question: How far back does David say his sin goes?

answers.text: To when his mother conceived him
To when he was anointed king

cards.text: Then David turns from what he's done to what God desires. It's truth, and David says exactly where God wants it.

cards.question: God desires truth. Where does David say God wants it?

cards.text: David says God teaches him wisdom in the inmost place. Then he asks God to purify him with hyssop so he'll be clean, and to wash him.

cards.question: True or false: David says that even after God washes him, a little of the stain will still show.

cards.text: Nope: whiter than snow. That's whiter than my apron at the START of a batch, and friend, that apron does NOT stay white past the first scoop of chocolate chips.
Then David talks about his bones, the bones God has crushed.

cards.question: With his bones crushed, what does David ask God to let him hear?
David asks God to let his crushed bones rejoice. Then he asks God to hide His face from something. What is it?

cards.text: So far, David's asked God to wash away what he did. Now he asks for something bigger than a cleanup.

cards.question: David asks God to create something in him. What?

cards.text: Create, friend, not patch. That's not scraping the burnt edges off an old cookie, that's a whole new batch, and he asks God to renew a right spirit in him too.
Then David asks God for two things NOT to happen.

cards.question: First, David asks God not to cast him away. Away from what?
True or false: David also asks God not to take His Holy Spirit from him.

cards.text: Then David asks God to give something back. I bet he remembers exactly what it felt like.

cards.question: What does David ask God to restore to him?

cards.text: He asks God to sustain him with a willing spirit. Then David looks past himself, to other people who've gone wrong.

cards.question: David says he'll teach transgressors God's ways, and sinners will ___ to God.

cards.text: Then David uses a heavy word. He asks God, the God of his salvation, to deliver him from bloodguilt.

cards.question: If God delivers him from bloodguilt, what does David say his tongue will do?

cards.text: Then David asks God to open his lips, and his mouth will declare God's praise. I went years in that drawer barely saying a word, and now I talk so much my ovens need a vacation.
Now David turns to sacrifice and burnt offerings.

cards.question: True or false: At this point, David says God delights in sacrifice, so a sacrifice is what he'll bring.
If not burnt offerings, what does David say the sacrifices of God are?
True or false: David says God will turn away a broken and contrite heart.
At the end, David prays for more than himself. He asks God to cause Zion to prosper. What does he ask God to build up?
A few lines back, God took no pleasure in burnt offerings. Once Jerusalem is built up, what kind of sacrifices does David say God will delight in?

findings.problem: Story card 14 already says David asks God to purify him 'so he'll be clean.' That gives away the answer to the true or false question about whether a stain will still show. It also rules out the True answer before the baker picks.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The 'reply all' joke makes the baker the one who messed up ('that reply all you sent to the whole office by mistake'). When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it should be Papa Dorin himself, not the baker.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: Both stops follow the same question-type pattern. Stop 1 runs MC, MC, TF, MC, FB, MC, MC, TF, MC, MC. Stop 2 runs MC, MC, TF, MC, FB, MC, TF, MC, TF, MC, MC. The first five choice cards in each stop match exactly.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 7 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'Larger sacrifices' and 'Costlier sacrifices' aren't clearly false in the passage. Psalm 51:19 goes on to name whole burnt offerings and bulls offered on the altar, and a baker could argue those are larger and costlier sacrifices.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Only the right answer, 'The joy of His salvation', uses a capitalized 'His' pointing to God. The wrong answers use a lowercase 'his' pointing to David. The capital letter makes the right answer stand out as the one about God.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The psalm's closing turn is never told. In Psalm 51:19, God will delight in whole burnt offerings and bulls will be offered on His altar, which is the counterpoint to verse 16. The walkthrough ends on the choice card about righteous sacrifices, and no card tells the rest of the verse, so the baker misses an important detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
